newsitem.title: USA: AIG Q2 foreign general premiums down.
newsitem.headline: AIG Q2 foreign general premiums down.

text.p: American International Group Inc said second quarter net premiums written in its foreign general insurance business declined 1.4 percent, after the impact of foreign exchange.
Before the impact of foreign exchange, second quarter net premiums written rose 5.1 percent in the foreign general business.

"Premium growth in original currency was strong in Continental Europe and Latin America, and in Japan exceeded the industry," AIG chairman Maurice Greenberg said. "In addition, operating income was very strong," he said.
However, he said, the London market continues to reflect U.S. conditions in terms of pricing, and AIG's strategy there mirrors its U.S. focus on specialty and niche products.
"In Thailand, economic conditions had an impact on growth in the quarter, but we do not expect this to be long lasting," Greenberg said.

In addition, he said, many new initiatives are underway in AIG's foreign general business, both in new products and methods of distribution, that will lead to even stronger performance in future periods.
During the quarter, he said, AIG announced an expansion of AIG South Africa's distribution of consumer insurance products through a joint venture with a major local institution.
In addition, AIG launched direct auto operations in Israel in the second quarter, and shortly after the quarter's close, in Brazil.

In general insurance, worldwide net premiums written after the impact of foreign exchange rose 5.3 percent from a year ago. Before the impact of foreign exchange, worldwide general insurance net premiums written rose 7.5 percent.
The company achieved an underwriting profit of $134.5 million in worldwide general insurance and a combined ratio of 95.92 compared with 95.98 a year ago.
